summary: Asked by Pharisees when God’s kingdom will come, Jesus says it does not come with signs to watch for, then warns His disciples that His day will come suddenly.
key_insight: Jesus gives two audiences two answers. To the Pharisees, watching for the kingdom’s arrival, He says it is already present: “the kingdom of God is within you.” To the disciples He says the day of the Son of Man is still to come, as sudden as lightning. The kingdom is here, and its day is coming.
story: Some Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come. He answered, “The kingdom of God does not come with observation; nor will they say, ‘See here!’ or ‘See there!’ For indeed, the kingdom of God is within you.”

Then He turned to His disciples. “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.” People would say, ‘Look here!’ or ‘Look there!’, but they must not follow them. The Son of Man in His day would be like lightning flashing from one side of the sky to the other. “But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.”

His day would come as the flood came in the days of Noah. People ate and drank, married and were given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark and the flood destroyed them all. It would be as in the days of Lot: they bought and sold, planted and built, until the day Lot went out of Sodom and fire and brimstone rained from heaven. “Even so will it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed.”

In that day no one on the housetop should go down for his goods, and no one in the field should turn back. “Remember Lot’s wife. Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life will preserve it.”
That night two would be in one bed, two women grinding grain together, two men in the field; in each pair, “the one will be taken and the other left.”
The disciples asked, “Where, Lord?” He answered, “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together.”

fit.question: Much of this teaching, the lightning, the days of Noah, the housetop and the field, one taken and the other left, appears again in Matthew 24, in Jesus’ last discourse on the Mount of Olives. Did Luke move it, or did Jesus say it twice?

points.label: Luke records both occasions
points.text: Luke tells this teaching here, on the road, and then gives his own account of the Mount of Olives discourse in chapter 21, with different material. He plainly understood them as two separate times of teaching.

points.label: A teacher repeats His warnings
points.text: Jesus taught for about three years in many places. Central warnings, like the days of Noah, would naturally be given more than once, in words that partly match and partly differ.

fit.note: Repeated sayings are what we would expect from a traveling teacher; nothing here requires an error.
fit.short: Jesus gave these warnings on the road (Luke 17) and again on the Mount of Olives (Matthew 24). Luke himself records both occasions.

scene.label: “Within you”
scene.text: The Greek phrase can mean within you, in the heart, or in your midst, among you. Jesus was speaking to Pharisees, so many read it as among you: the King was standing in front of them. Others take it as God’s rule in the heart. On either reading the kingdom was not something to wait for with a calendar.

scene.label: Lot’s wife
scene.text: The angels led Lot’s wife out of Sodom by the hand, yet she looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:16, 26). Jesus uses her as a warning against clinging to what is being left behind.

scene.label: Grinding together
scene.text: Grinding grain at a hand mill was daily work, often done by two women sharing one mill. Jesus pictures the most ordinary moments of home and field, interrupted.

scene.label: Eagles
scene.text: The Greek word can mean eagles or vultures. Birds gathering over a body was a familiar sight and a proverb (compare Job 39:30): when judgment comes, it will be as plain as circling vultures.

scene.label: Verse 36
scene.text: Many of the oldest manuscripts of Luke do not have verse 36, about two men in the field. The NKJV includes it. The same saying appears in Matthew 24:40.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke records the Pharisees’ question and the two-part answer. He alone sets Lot beside Noah and adds the command, “Remember Lot’s wife.” As he does throughout the journey to Jerusalem, Luke keeps the cross in view: in the middle of a teaching about glory, Jesus says He must first suffer (v. 25).

seeing.reveals: Jesus speaks of His coming as the day of the Son of Man, visible across the whole sky, and in the same breath says He must first suffer and be rejected. The King of that day is the King of the cross.
seeing.living: Jesus does not satisfy curiosity about dates. He warns against holding this life so tightly that you turn back for it, as Lot’s wife did. Hold the house, the field and the goods loosely enough to leave them without looking back.
seeing.ponder: What in your life would make you turn and look back if the Son of Man came today?

preaching.big_idea: The kingdom has come in Jesus; His day will come suddenly. Do not look back.
outline: A day no one will miss (22–25)
A heart that will not look back (31–37)
preaching.watch_for: The words “day” and “days” run through the passage (vv. 22, 24, 26–31). Jesus sets the ordinary days of eating, buying and building beside the one day when the Son of Man is revealed.
